met_analysis:
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Anupgarh, Delhi, Shahjahanpur, Basti, Chapra and thence eastwards towards Nagaland.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 68°E to the north of Lat. 32°N.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over North Haryana & neighbourhoodbetween 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The cyclonic circulation over Northeast Rajasthan & neighbourhood persists and now extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central parts of south Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood persists and now seen at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Bihar & neighbourhood between 1.5 &3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood persists and now extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Saurashtra & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Interior Karnataka & neighbourhoodat 5.8 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Westcentral Bay of Bengal & adjoining Coastal Andhra Pradesh at 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
